Questions
Do I need an account?
No. ContextFlow works right after you turn it on in Safari. Subscriptions are tied to your Apple Account and work on all your devices.
Which AI does ContextFlow use?

Answers come from Anthropic's Claude, and from OpenAI when Claude is unavailable. Google answers use Google Search through Gemini, and Listen uses Google's Gemini voices. With the Own key plan you use your own OpenAI or Claude key. Page text is sent only when you ask something and is not used to train models.
What does Ultra add to Pro?

Listen, which reads answers and whole pages aloud (30 minutes a week); Find similar, which finds checked alternatives to any page (10 searches a week); and up to 50 watched pages instead of 20. Moving up from Pro starts at once, and Apple refunds what's left of Pro.
Does it work on every website?
On regular websites, yes. Safari doesn't let extensions read some pages (the start page, App Store pages, PDFs in some cases) — you can still ask general questions there.

Your plan
On all your devices
Started on iPhone, finishing on Mac? Turn on Sync chats with iCloud, and a chat continues on your iPad and Mac. It's end-to-end encrypted in your iCloud and never stored on my server.
Waiting on a lot of prices at once? Ultra watches up to 50 pages, against 20 on Pro and 5 on Free. Everything else about watching stays the same.

Open it on the page you're reading and ask. No prompts to write.
Open it on any page
Where is it? On iPhone and iPad, tap ✦ on the page, or open the page menu in the address bar and choose ContextFlow. On Mac, click ✦ or the ContextFlow icon in the toolbar, or press Control-Shift-E.
Move ✦ out of the way
Is the ✦ button covering what you're reading? Drag it up or down along the edge, or over to the other side, and it stays there.
One tap for the gist
Long article and no time? Summarize, Key takeaways, Explain simply and Translate work on the whole page. You don't have to write a prompt.
Ask about a part
Only one paragraph is confusing? Select it and choose Ask AI. The answer is about that part only. It can also explain, translate or rewrite it.
Ask or note a selection
Found a line worth keeping? Select it and tap Note: it goes into the chat with its page. Or type your own question about it right under the selection. Notes don't use answers.
Quick actions under a selection

Don't feel like typing on your phone? On iPhone and iPad, select text, and the “Your question…” field under it holds Summarize, Translate, Find similar and more. Swipe along them and tap one. On Mac, it's the same field: scroll along it with the trackpad or the mouse wheel and click one.
A chat follows you
Reading across several pages? Keep asking as you go. The chat remembers the conversation and which page each question was about. Tap a page's name in the chat to go back to it.
Fresh facts from Google
Need something recent? Turn on Google next to the question field, and the answer comes from Google Search with its sources: news, prices, anything new.
The small things that turn a chat into a notebook for what you read.
Notes of your own
Have a thought, not a question? Swipe the send button up or down (on Mac, scroll on it) to write a note instead. It stays in the chat with its page and doesn't use answers.
Highlight what matters
One line in an answer is the one you need? Select it and tap Highlight. It stays marked, like with a pen. Later answers in the chat take your highlights into account, and Copy keeps them in bold.
Pinned at the top
Lost a good answer in a long chat? Pin it, and it waits in the bar at the top of the chat. Tap the bar to jump to it, tap again for the next one.
Swipe to pin or delete
On iPhone and iPad, swipe an answer or a note to the right to pin it, to the left to delete it. On Mac, point at it and the same buttons show beside it. Changed your mind? Undo brings it back.
The whole chat in mind

Want an answer that uses everything you collected? Turn on Whole chat under the question field: every message, your notes and the other pages of this chat go with the question. Off, it's the last messages and the open page.
Ask about a video Pro

Don't want to watch the whole thing to find one part? ContextFlow reads the video's transcript. Ask for the gist, or what was said about something, and the answer points to the moment, like [4:15]. On Free, answers use the page's text.
PDFs on the page Pro

The details are in a PDF? PDFs shown on the page or linked from it go with your question, and the answer says which page of the PDF it's from. On iPad and Mac it works on a PDF tab too. On Free, answers use the page's text.

Wondering what else is out there? Tap Find similar in the panel, or select a product's name and tap Find similar under it. Add a condition like Cheaper or In stock if you want. Every alternative is a real page, opened and checked before you see it.

Rather listen than read? Tap Listen under an answer, or choose Listen to this page in the … menu. A natural voice reads it at 1×, 1.2×, 1.5× or 2×. On iPhone and iPad it plays in the ContextFlow app and keeps going with the screen locked; on Mac, right in the panel.
For forms, replies and anything you keep typing again.
Insert into any field

Typing the same things into forms? Tap a text field on a page, then the ContextFlow button by it: what you copied in other tabs, your templates and the last answer are one tap away. With a keyboard, type / and a few words of a template, then Tab. On Mac, Control-Shift-V opens the whole list.
Copied, kept for a day

Copied something three tabs ago, then copied over it? The last things you copied on pages in Safari wait in the list for a day, on this device only. Nothing from password or card fields, and nothing in Private Browsing.
Templates that fill themselves

Same reply every time, only the name and the date change? Select it and tap Template: ContextFlow marks what changes. When you insert it, Fill from the page puts them in, highlighted so you can check.
The bell is about time: come back when you choose. The eye is about a change: hear about it when it happens.
Remind me about this page

Want to finish reading tonight? Select a line and tap the bell, or tap … at the top of the panel, then Remind me about this page…, and pick a time. The reminder opens this page. Answers and notes have Remind me in their … menu.
Know when a price drops

Waiting for a sale or for something to be back in stock? Select the price, the stock status or a date and tap the eye. For the whole page, choose Watch this page… in the … menu at the top of the panel. ContextFlow checks the page while you use Safari and tells you when it changes, or drops below the price you name.
Find an old chat, keep topics apart, take your chats to your other devices.
Start fresh or go back
New topic? Start a new chat with +. Earlier chats wait in the chat list: open one to pick up where you left off, rename it with the pencil, or delete it.
Search your chats
Remember a word but not the chat? Type it in the search over the chat list: every chat with it shows up, with the place it's in, and a result opens the chat right there.
Tags and folders
Work and home in one list? Tag a chat, an answer or a note with 🏷. Tap a tag to see only its chats, or turn on Folders to group the list by tag.
Share what you found
Sending it to someone? Share one answer or the whole chat. The text comes with its links, its sources and a link to ContextFlow.
Your chats in the app

Want to read a chat away from Safari? The ContextFlow app has every chat. Ask about its pages or add a note right there, tag, copy or share any answer. Continue in Safari picks it up where you left off.
AI search Pro
Remember what a chat was about, but none of its words? Tap ✦ next to the search and describe it, like “that article about sleep and coffee”.
Ask your chats Pro
“What did I read this week?” The first row of the chat list answers from all your chats at once. Try “Summarize my notes on AI”.
Where it belongs Pro
Asked about a car in the chat about a sofa? Under the answer, ContextFlow suggests the chat it belongs in, or a new one. One tap moves it there; Undo puts it back.
Your tags, suggested Pro
Tired of tagging by hand? ContextFlow learns what your tags mean from where you put them, and suggests one under a new answer or note. Only your own tags, and only when one fits.
How you pay for it, and what your plan adds.
Monthly or yearly

Want to pay less? Pro and Ultra come monthly or yearly, and a year costs less than twelve months. Tap Yearly above the plans to see each price and what you save. Already on monthly? Switch to yearly is in Settings → Your plan, and it starts when your current month ends.
What your plan adds

Just upgraded and not sure what's new? After you buy Pro or Ultra, ContextFlow shows what your plan adds, a step at a time. To see it again, tap … at the top of the panel, then Other… and What's in Pro or What's in Ultra. In the app, it's in Settings, under Your plan.
Make it fit you, and know what leaves your device.
Tell it about you
Want answers that fit you? Add a line under About me, like what you do or how you like answers, and ContextFlow takes it into account.
Hide ✦ when you don't need it
Don't need the ✦ button on a site? Hide it there, or turn it off everywhere in the extension settings. ContextFlow still opens from Safari's extensions menu.
Use your own API key
Have an OpenAI or Claude key? With Pro or the Own key plan, paste it in the extension settings in Safari, and requests go straight to that provider.
Private by design

What gets sent? ContextFlow reads a page only when you ask, and sends just its text to get the answer. Your chats stay on your devices and in your iCloud. With suggestions on, the text of new messages also goes to my server to find where they belong; I don't keep it.

Clipboard history and reply templates for Safari on iPhone, iPad and Mac — ContextFlow

Typing the same replies every day? ContextFlow keeps what you copied in Safari for a day, turns a reply you sent into a template that fills in the name and the date from the page, and puts it into any text field.
Replies and forms in Safari, without retyping
What you copied in other tabs, and templates that fill in the name and the date from the page, in any text field in Safari.
Typing the same replies every day?
Does it see everything I copy?

No. Only what you copy on web pages in Safari. It skips password and card fields and Private Browsing, keeps things for a day on this device only, and you can clear the list or turn Copied off in settings.
Where are my templates kept?
On your devices, and in your iCloud if sync is on. When you tap Fill from the page, the template and the page's text go to my server to find the values. Nothing is kept there.
Does it work on Mac?
Yes. Type / and a few words of a template in any field, then press Tab, or press Control-Shift-V to open the list.
Is it free?
Copied, templates and inserting are free. Filling blanks from the page works a few times a day on Free, and as often as you need with Pro.

Forms you fill in every week

Company details, a delivery address, the standard description of what you sell. Save each one as a template once, and it's one tap away in any field on any site. With a keyboard on iPad or Mac, type / and a few words of the template, then press Tab. On Mac, Control-Shift-V opens the whole list. A reply that depends on the page

Someone sent a long message, or you're answering about a listing or a document. Open ContextFlow on that page and ask for a draft: “a short, polite no”, “answer her three questions”. Under the answer, Insert into field puts it into the reply box. Read it before you send it.
Answers and Insert into field. Free to start; if you ask a lot, Pro gives you more answers.
Where it won't help
It lives in Safari. What you copy in other apps doesn't show up in Copied, and in Mail or Messages there's no ContextFlow button.
It isn't a keyboard or a clipboard for the whole phone. If that's what you need, this isn't it.
A few fields don't accept text from extensions. Then ContextFlow copies it and tells you, and you paste it yourself.

Copied, templates, the button by the field, / and Tab, Insert into field. Fill from the page a few times a day.

Yes. Safari on iPhone runs extensions, and an AI extension can read the page you have open and answer questions about it, right there, with no copying and pasting. I make one called ContextFlow. Here's what it does, how to turn it on, and where it falls short.
What it does with the page you're reading
Tap the ✦ button on any page. It floats at the edge of the screen on iPhone and iPad.
Pick Summarize, Key takeaways, Explain or Translate, or type your own question: “What's the catch?”, “Is this source reliable?”, “What do I do next?”
Select a paragraph first, and the answer is about that part only.
The answer is about the page you're on. You don't copy anything or switch apps.
With Ultra, tap Listen to hear an answer or the whole page in a natural voice, or Find similar for alternatives to what you're looking at.
It keeps what you read, not just what you asked
This is the part I use most. A chat isn't stuck to one page. It carries on as you go from page to page, and it keeps three things together:
The pages you read in it. Each chat lists its pages; tap one to go back to it.
The answers you asked for.
Your own notes. Swipe the send button up or down and it turns into “Save note”. A note stays in the chat next to its page and uses no answers.

So a chat ends up as your notes and your browsing history on one topic, in one place. Pin the chats you come back to, and rename them. Turn on “Sync chats with iCloud” and the same chat is on your iPad and Mac too. More on this in keeping notes while you read.
What people use it for most, with clips: replies and forms, studying a topic, shopping and planning over several days.
How to turn it on
Install ContextFlow from the App Store and open the app once. It walks you through the next step.
Open the Settings app → Apps → Safari → Extensions → ContextFlow. Switch it on and set All Websites to Allow.
Open any website in Safari and tap ✦. You can also open it from the page menu in the address bar.
On Mac: Safari → Settings → Extensions, tick ContextFlow, then click its icon in the toolbar or press Control-Shift-E.
Where it falls short
Safari doesn't let extensions read some pages, like the start page and App Store pages. You can still ask general questions there.
It lives in Safari. If you browse in Chrome on your iPhone, it won't be there.
Answers come from an AI model online, so it needs a connection. And AI can be wrong: check anything important.
It's free to start. If you ask a lot, you'll want Pro, which gives you more answers, and deeper ones. Ultra adds listening and Find similar.
If all you want is the gist of an article, Safari's own summary may be enough. I compared the options honestly in Safari's summary vs ChatGPT vs an extension.
Privacy, briefly
No account and no sign-up.
A page is read only when you ask about it. Page text isn't stored on my server.
Chats stay on your devices. iCloud sync is end-to-end encrypted. Details are in the Privacy Policy.

There are three common ways to get AI help with the page you're reading on an iPhone, iPad or Mac. I make one of them, ContextFlow, so keep that in mind. Each of the three has its place, and I'll say where the other two are the better pick.
Safari's own summary
On devices with Apple Intelligence, Safari can summarize an article: open Reader from the address bar and tap Summarize.
Good: free, built in, nothing to install.

Limits: it needs Apple Intelligence on your device, in a supported language and region. It works on pages that open in Reader. It gives you a summary, not a conversation, and it doesn't keep anything for later.
Pick it when: you have a recent iPhone, iPad or Mac and just want the gist of an article.
Apple keeps adding Apple Intelligence features, so check what your version of iOS or macOS does.
Copying the page into ChatGPT
Copy the text or the link, open ChatGPT, paste, ask.
Good: strong models, a free tier, and room for a long back-and-forth. It can also search the web.

Limits: you switch apps every time. On iPhone, selecting a whole article is fiddly. If you paste only the link, ChatGPT can't see pages you're signed in to or that sit behind a paywall. And the chat doesn't know which page a question came from unless you paste the link again.
Pick it when: the question isn't really about one page, or you're settling in for a long research session in ChatGPT anyway.

Good: no copying and no app switching. It reads the page as it is in your Safari, so a page you're signed in to works too. Select a paragraph to ask about just that. A chat carries on from page to page and keeps the pages you read, the answers you asked for and your own notes together, on iPhone, iPad and Mac.

Limits: Safari only. Safari doesn't let extensions read some pages, like the start page and App Store pages. Answers come from an AI model online, so you need a connection. It's free to start, and if you ask a lot you'll want Pro.

Getting started
How do I turn on ContextFlow on iPhone or iPad?

Open the Settings app → Apps → Safari → Extensions → ContextFlow, switch it on and set All Websites to Allow. Then open any website in Safari and tap the ✦ button (or the page menu in the address bar → ContextFlow).
How do I turn it on on Mac?
Open Safari → Settings → Extensions and tick ContextFlow, then allow it on all websites. Click the ContextFlow icon in the toolbar or press Control-Shift-E on any page.
Nothing happens when I tap the button

Make sure ContextFlow is allowed on the site (Safari's page menu → ContextFlow → Always Allow on Every Website). Some pages can't be read by extensions (Safari's start page, App Store pages); open a regular website instead. Reloading the page after enabling the extension also helps.
Plans and subscriptions
How many free answers do I get?
5 answers every day, renewed at midnight UTC. No account is needed.
I subscribed, but ContextFlow still shows the free plan
Open the ContextFlow app once (it shares your subscription with the extension), then reopen the panel in Safari. If needed, tap Restore Purchases on the Pro screen.
Does one subscription work on all my devices?
Yes — on every iPhone, iPad and Mac signed in to the same Apple Account. Open the ContextFlow app once on each device.
How do I cancel?
iPhone/iPad: Settings → your name → Subscriptions → ContextFlow. Mac: App Store → your name → Account Settings → Subscriptions. You keep access until the end of the paid period.
How do I use my own OpenAI or Claude key?

With the Pro or Own key plan, open the ContextFlow panel in Safari → Settings → Own API key and paste an OpenAI key (sk-…) or an Anthropic key (sk-ant-…). Under Model, pick Fast (newest Claude Haiku or GPT mini) or Smart (newest Claude Sonnet or GPT). Requests then go directly from your device to that provider.
Privacy
What is sent when I ask a question?
Your question and the page text (or your selection) — only at that moment, only to generate the answer. Details in the Privacy Policy.

E-mail us from the address you signed up with and we'll delete it within 30 days. Version 2.0 no longer uses accounts.
